engagement_title: Verranza Coastal Retreats: bring three villas shot on two trips by two people into one collection, and build the presentation, the booking pages and the twelve in villa season cards off it, recover the collection's hand inked cove mark as artwork the vendors can use, and cut the welcome things onto its own ground
vertical: Real Estate, Construction and Property, luxury vacation rental portfolio, three villas on a fictional stretch of the southern French coast
real_brief_anchor: Anchor: the Upwork real estate finishing brief quoted in the ledger, posted by a boutique vacation rental manager asking for a consistent premium visual identity across the whole portfolio with a natural, realistic look, and carrying an explicit do not want list: no fake high dynamic range, no over saturation, no unrealistically blue pools. That post named no company, place or vendor, so the collection is laundered to the fictional Verranza Coastal Retreats on the fictional cove of Anse Verranza on the southern French coast, with the invented villas Solane, Cascina and Aubine. This is a REBUILD rather than a strengthen. The killed original ran three independent short imaging passes and finished there, which is a finishing job rather than a commission and sat on one surface. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes what the honest fuller version is, because the finishing pass is only the front half of what this client actually needs: HTML authoring now produces a native editable multi root document at mixed canvas sizes, so the presentation and the booking pages are real deliverables, and a bare press PDF from their printer can be reverse engineered into a live merge template, so the twelve in villa season cards become a genuine record per page run whose photographs are the very frames the finishing pass produced. That dependency, a badly finished frame being invisible until it lands in the card at the card's crop, is what turns three separate passes into one engagement. The same capabilities change the imaging half too: the collection's only graphic mark, a hand inked cove motif that survives as a scan and as an etch on one villa's door glass, can be recovered as real vector rather than redrawn, and the contractual welcome provision the client leaves in every house can be isolated onto the collection's own ground, so the raster surface is a full imaging engagement rather than a grade and crop pass.
client_one_liner: Three villas, two trips, two people behind the camera and a second batch someone else already worked on, and put on one screen they look like three different holidays.
client_brief:
Verranza Coastal Retreats

We manage three villas on a quiet stretch of the southern French coast: Villa Solane, Villa Cascina and Maison Aubine. Between eighteen hundred and four thousand two hundred a night depending on season. Our guests are forty to sixty five and they take the whole villa for a birthday, an anniversary, or three generations at once. They compare us against hotels, so we are held to a hotel's standard of consistency and we do not meet it.

The problem is that we look like three separate rentals. The photography came from two trips a year apart with two different people behind the camera, and the second batch came back already worked on by an editor we no longer use. Put the three villas on one screen and they are three different holidays.

What we want the pictures to look like. Natural. What the house actually looks like at that hour. We do not want the fake high dynamic range look, we do not want everything saturated, and above all we do not want the pool water turned a blue that does not exist. We have lost bookings over exactly that. Warm stone, real shadow, restraint.

What we need built. One presentation we can send to a travel agency or a private client, covering the collection, then each villa, then what is included, then how the rates ladder through the year. The pages that sit behind each villa's booking link, with the amenity list as a proper table. And the posts we run when a season opens. All editable, because rates change twice a year and we cannot come back to you each time.

And the in villa card. Our printer has our artwork. Each villa gets one per season with that season's rate, minimum stay and the season note, so twelve cards, each with the right villa on the front.

Two more things about the look. We leave the same welcome in every house, the local rose, a loaf, the estate oil and a bowl of figs, and on the page that says what is included we want those cut out clean on our own paper colour, not another room shot. And the little cove drawing an artist made for us when we opened, the one etched on Maison Aubine's door glass and stamped on the card, our foil printer and the glass people both keep asking us for a proper file and all we have is the scan of the inking. Make us one that still looks drawn by hand.

A short note on the look, the type, and anything we should know.
price_band_and_audience: Villas at 1,800 to 4,200 dollars a night, guests 40 to 65 booking whole property stays for a milestone, comparing the collection against hotels rather than against other rentals. The band is load bearing. At this price the grammar is generous negative space, full bleed architecture allowed to be quiet, rates carried in a discreet table rather than announced, and photography that is believable before it is impressive, because the guest who pays 4,200 a night has been to the actual house and will recognise a lie in the water. Push it down into a bargain rental grid of eight thumbnails, a price badge and a book now block and the collection reads as an aggregator listing and the rate stops being defensible. Push it further up into pure sparseness with the rates hidden entirely and a travel agency cannot sell from it. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even with every technical gate green. A real posted job of this shape runs 1,800 to 4,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: The whole house, the whole coast.
brand_identity.sector: Boutique luxury vacation-rental collection managing whole-property villas on the southern French coast.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2016, on the cove of Anse Verranza, southern French coast. A small management team, three villas.
brand_identity.about: Verranza Coastal Retreats manages three whole-property villas, Villa Solane, Villa Cascina and Maison Aubine, on a quiet stretch of the southern French coast. Guests take the entire villa for a milestone, and the collection is held to a hotel's standard of consistency because that is what its guests compare it against.
brand_identity.audience: Guests aged 40 to 65 booking a whole villa for a birthday, an anniversary or a multi-generation gathering, plus the travel agencies and private clients who book on their behalf. They have stayed in the real houses and will recognise anything that is not true.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Villas run 1,800 to 4,200 dollars a night depending on season, positioned against boutique hotels rather than other rentals. The grammar is generous space and quiet architecture, with rates carried in a discreet table rather than announced, so the collection never reads as an aggregator listing.
brand_identity.typography: One quiet prestige system: an elegant high-contrast serif for display and villa names, set with air, paired with a clean humanist sans for amenity tables, the rate ladder and body. Restraint over flourish, so it reads considered without tipping into fashion-house coldness a family will not book from.
brand_identity.voice: Calm, warm, understated. Describes what the house actually is at that hour, never oversells. Example line: "Warm stone, a long terrace, and the pool in real afternoon light."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The collection has a printed in-villa season card whose artwork is held by its printer as a press PDF, and a written owner note recording what the previous editor got wrong. There is no lost wordmark here; the constraint is photographic consistency across three villas shot on two trips by two people, with the second batch already worked on by an editor no longer used. The collection's one graphic mark is a small hand inked cove motif an artist drew for the founders, which survives only as a flatbed scan of the original inking and as the mark etched on Maison Aubine's door glass; it has never been redrawn or digitised, and the foil printer and the glass etcher need it as vector artwork. The contractual welcome provision left in every house exists only as a short still life set the manager shot on a villa's limestone counter.
brand_identity.values: Believable before impressive. One collection, not three holidays. Natural light, real shadow, honest water, and no fake high dynamic range or dyed pools.

assets_supplied.name: verranza_captures/ (21 frames across three villas, 6720 x 4480)
assets_supplied.kind: Architectural and interior capture of all three villas, gathered on two trips a year apart by two different photographers, delivered as a single folder with villa prefixes.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything we have for the three houses. The second trip came back already worked on by an editor we no longer use."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The second trip's frames arrived with a finishing curve already baked in, so they carry contrast that fights a global correction and their pool water already sits near the ceiling of its channel, which is precisely the look the manager rules out and which a moderate move cannot walk all the way back. Separately two of the twenty one are the same terrace from one tripod position a minute apart, so one villa reaches the presentation a frame short of what the folder count suggests.

assets_supplied.name: verranza_season_card.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The collection's existing in villa season card exactly as its printer holds it: a real press PDF, one card per page, a photograph panel at the top and then the season name, the nightly rate, the minimum stay and a short season note set as printed type.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our printer's file. We just want each villa and each season dropped into it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The season note frame on the printed sheet was sized to the shortest specimen the printer happened to set, and it is a fixed frame: a merged record longer than that does not spill and does not reflow, it simply stops rendering at the frame edge, so the page returns successfully with the sentence cut off at trim. The printed face also reads as separate blocks that the conversion does not necessarily expose as separate frames.

assets_supplied.name: verranza_rates.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Twelve rows: villa, season, nightly rate, minimum stay, and the season note that goes on the card, plus a column naming the villa photograph for each row.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Rates as they stand for the coming year. Twelve cards, three villas by four seasons."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: One villa's shoulder season note runs two lines longer than every other record, and the minimum stay column is written three different ways across the twelve rows. Neither is visible from the file's shape, and the photograph column names only three distinct files for twelve rows.

assets_supplied.name: verranza_amenities.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text: the per villa amenity list, bed and bath counts, sleeping capacity, the included services, and the four season definitions with their date ranges.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What goes in the amenity table on each villa's page. The included services list is contractual."

assets_supplied.name: verranza_owner_note.png
assets_supplied.kind: Screengrab of the manager's own written note to the previous editor, listing what went wrong last time.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What we told the last person. Please read it before you start."

assets_supplied.name: verranza_welcome_stills/ (6 still life frames, 6720 x 4480)
assets_supplied.kind: A short still life set the manager shot of the welcome provision that is contractual with every whole house stay: the local rose, a boule of village bread, a jar of the estate olive oil, a bowl of figs and a folded linen bundle, each photographed on the warm limestone of a villa counter for the what is included section.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The welcome things we leave in every house, shot on the kitchen stone. We want them cut out clean on our own paper colour for the included page, not another room shot."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The rose, the clear glass, the pale crust and the honey oil all sit within a hair of the warm limestone they are shot on, so a one call subject knockout returns a clean looking complete cutout that has quietly bitten the pale glass shoulder or the crust edge where object and stone share value, and the bite is invisible until the cutout is placed on the Linen brand ground rather than on white. The bowl of figs, being dark, knocks out cleanly, so the route is a per frame decision rather than a global one, and two of the six are the same bottle from one position so the set lands one distinct object short of its count.

assets_supplied.name: verranza_cove_mark.png
assets_supplied.kind: A flatbed scan of the collection's only graphic mark: a small hand inked line drawing of the Anse Verranza cove, a stylised headland, the cove mouth and a single villa roofline, drawn for the founders by a local artist. Supplied as a high contrast scan of the original inking on off white paper; there is no vector version anywhere.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The little cove drawing from when we opened. It is etched on Maison Aubine's door glass and stamped on the card, and the vendors want a proper file. This scan is all we have."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The inked strokes carry hairline tapers and small enclosed counters, the cove mouth and the roofline's window openings, that a trace holds at full scan size and closes at the height the mark is actually reproduced, a thumbnail across the corner of the card and smaller again on the etched door glass. The aged ink and the warm off white paper run close in value across one edge of the sheet, so a selection naming the drawing rather than the ink returns the paper with it, and the scan is only modest resolution so the mark cannot be enlarged to buy back detail.

acceptance_bar: The three villas read as one collection when placed on one screen: one white point, one black point, one treatment of stone and shadow, one relationship between interior and exterior brightness. A frame that cannot be brought to the collection is named in the note, not shipped at eighty percent.
The water in every delivered frame is a colour that could exist at that hour in that place. A frame whose water reads as dyed fails regardless of how the rest of it looks.
No delivered file exceeds the pixel dimensions of the frame it came from, and no crop or knockout tradeoff record in the run carries an upscale entry.
Every villa is represented by distinct frames, and no frame stands in for two rooms or two villas.
Any licensed frame that joins the work sits inside the collection rather than beside it. A bought looking frame on the opening root fails.

The welcome detail objects sit isolated on the flat Linen brand ground with clear air at every edge, and the cut edge holds where the pale object meets the warm limestone when looked at close up rather than at thumbnail scale, with no object standing in for two.

The cove mark is delivered as placeable artwork rather than a picture of the scan: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, the mark still reading as the founders' hand, and every counter still open at the height it is foil stamped on the card and etched on the door glass, on those grounds rather than on white, with a stated safe minimum height.
The twelve season cards are one run, one record per page, at the card's true trim, each carrying its own villa's photograph, its own season, rate, minimum stay and season note.
Every season note is legible in full on its card. A note that ends mid sentence at the frame edge fails even though the page rendered successfully.
The minimum stay reads the same way on all twelve cards.

The presentation, the three booking pages and the social set are delivered as native editable documents with each canvas keeping its own size, live retypeable text, the amenity list and the rate ladder as real tables, and every photograph carried as embedded image data rather than a reference.
Type set over a photograph is legible on every canvas, not only on the one that can be previewed.
One type system across the presentation, the booking pages, the social set and the card, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual weight used.
The whole set reads as an 1,800 to 4,200 dollar a night collection judged against hotels: generous, quiet, believable. Neither an aggregator grid nor a rate free art piece.

The note records per photograph what was applied and why that frame differs from its neighbours, every resize any tool reported, what the card template actually contained, and anything the manager should know before rates change again.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted here and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_apply_auto_tone, image_adjust_light_portions, image_adjust_dark_portions, image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_select_subject, image_invert_selection, image_remove_background in both the transparent and backgroundColor forms, image_fill_area, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize reading metadata.tradeoffs and detection_confidence, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Every raster decision, and the half the client cares about most. It sets one collection target off the most honest natural frame and brings twenty one frames from two trips and two hands toward it one call at a time, walks the pre finished batch back rather than adding to it, confines the water and the greenery by selecting materials by their own visual properties rather than by the place they sit in, and cuts the presentation, booking page, social and card panel crops without ever enlarging. It also isolates the welcome provision onto the flat Linen ground, triaging the knockout route per still life between the one call subject route and a material named selection of the warm limestone inverted and filled where a pale object and pale stone share value, and recovers the hand inked cove mark at ink level with the vector hygiene the tracer does not perform for you.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (as generator and as validator), prepare_indd_merge_template with params.mappingJson passed as a JSON string, document_merge_data_layout with recordRange and additionalImageFiles, document_render_layout at real resolution
adobe_surfaces.role: The twelve in villa season cards as a genuine record per page run built from the printer's own PDF, which is the only surface in the connector that does variable data at volume. It requires reading the real frame inventory and the real story text out of the round tripped IDML before promising any mapping, binding the finished villa photographs per row through an image column, and rendering at real print resolution because the merge step ignores resolution on its own.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The portfolio presentation as multiple roots at one canvas size, the three booking pages and the social set as roots at their own sizes, all as native editable documents, which is the only surface here that composes free form fixed canvas layout. Every photograph must be pulled down and inlined as image data because a URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, the amenity lists and the rate ladder go in as real tables, family and weight are declared on every text element, and the payload goes by uploaded URL because inlined architectural photography passes the inline threshold immediately.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend called once per typographic role, font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The one type system carrying a presentation shown on a travel agency's screen, three booking pages, a social set and a printed card. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land on quiet prestige without tipping into fashion house coldness that a family of three generations will not book from. Numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, a display cut is reached by its own slug, and every name must be laundered into canonical PostScript form because one bad name kills the whole kit.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, SHORT query, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one frame the collection does not have, a coast or landscape band for the opening root, IP clean and at genuine camera scale with generative tech candidates excluded. The Boards half persists the selects set the three villa owners sign off from, placed within the twelve per call cap, with a partial success read as partial.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a pixel.
trajectory.judgement: The photography is raster work judged against a written do not want list, the presentation and booking pages have to be authored fixed canvas documents because rates change twice a year, and twelve cards at one record per page is a merge run. The welcome cutouts and the recovery of the cove mark are raster and vector work on the imaging surface, not authoring. The brief pins each destination.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by villa and role so that forty artefacts later the agent still knows which URL is which house.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by villa and role.

trajectory.action: Preview all twenty one villa frames and the six welcome still lifes and triage them: which villa, which room or aspect, which trip, which arrived already finished, which are duplicates of one another, which welcome object each still life shows and where object meets stone, and which frames each deliverable actually needs.
trajectory.judgement: The manager says two trips and two people. The pictures are the only place that can settle which frames were already worked on, and a pre finished frame has to be walked back rather than pushed further, which is the opposite move. The welcome set has to be read the same way: which object each frame is, which is a near duplicate, and where a pale object sits at the value of the stone it is on.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering villa, trip, prior processing, duplicates, and the shortfall it creates, plus a welcome set triage covering object, near duplicates and the object to stone value where a knockout will be decided.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop, and on architecture a leaning wall or a tilted waterline is the single tell that reads as an amateur listing.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Set one collection target off the most honest natural frame and bring each of the twenty one villa frames and the six welcome still lifes toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied per frame.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a collection, not three good houses. One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong across two trips, two hands and one already processed batch, so the agent holds one destination and reaches it by different routes.
trajectory.produces: Corrected masters at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Confined work on the water, the planting and the interior stone, selecting each by the material's own colour, surface and form rather than by the villa or the terrace it sits on, and judging every result against the manager's written do not want list.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the entire gate: naming the terrace pulls the selection to the terrace. And the do not want list is a design constraint, not a style note, so restraint has to be an active decision on the frames that arrived already pushed.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a global move would have taken the water synthetic or the stone grey.

trajectory.action: Cut every crop the collection needs: the full bleed presentation roots, the booking page heroes, the social ratios and the card's photograph panel ratio, reading the confidence and bounds each crop returns.
trajectory.judgement: A full bleed architectural root and a small card panel want different parts of the same frame, and the card panel is where a crop failure becomes a print run.
trajectory.produces: The full crop set at spec, each recorded against its source frame's dimensions.

trajectory.action: Cut the welcome detail cutouts: knock each of the graded welcome still lifes onto the flat Linen brand ground at the size the what is included panel and the season social set give them, triaging the route per frame between the one call subject knockout and a material named selection of the warm limestone inverted and filled, reading every returned tradeoff record rather than the success message.
trajectory.judgement: The tradeoff array is the only channel that reports what a tool did to a frame's dimensions and it carries no warning language, and a knockout on a pale object against pale stone can bite the edge on some frames and not others. Optical centring on a bottle or a boule is not geometric centring.
trajectory.produces: Welcome objects isolated on the brand ground with their returned tradeoffs recorded, and the knockout route stated per frame.

trajectory.action: Recover the cove mark: an ink level selection naming the paint's own visual properties rather than the paper it sits on, correct polarity, a bounds crop driven by the selection's own returned bounds, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas ground path removed, producing a single colour stamping and etching version and a colour accurate variant.
trajectory.judgement: Naming the substrate pulls the selection to the paper, background removal is the wrong instrument on inked strokes with counters, and the tracer takes no options at all, so every lever is in the raster preparation.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent cove mark plus a colour accurate variant.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for the coast or landscape band the opening root needs, filter to photography, exclude generative tech results, license and download at full resolution, then place it beside the three finished villas.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the collection target, not the prettiest thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale frame and a first honest read of it against the finished set.

trajectory.action: Create the selects board and add the finished set and any licensed frame within the per call placement cap, re sending only the entries the response names as failed.
trajectory.judgement: A 201 is partial success, and three separate owners have to sign off on what represents their house, so the board is a real deliverable rather than plumbing.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit for the whole collection.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a collection compared to hotels by a forty to sixty five year old booking a milestone. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Convert the printer's season card PDF, export the IDML, and read the real frame inventory, the real bounds and the real story text before promising any mapping.
trajectory.judgement: What the printed face looks like says nothing about what the conversion exposes, and the mapping strategy is entirely different for separated blocks than for one continuous flow. Looking first is the only honest way to justify a mapping.
trajectory.produces: A frame inventory with integer page item ids, bounds and applied type, plus the story text reconstructed from the IDML content runs.

trajectory.action: Build the mapping against the reconstructed story text, run it through the validator, prepare the merge template, reshape the data so the photograph column can actually bind, then round trip the IDML again and confirm every expected placeholder is present.
trajectory.judgement: Neither a VALID verdict nor a success message is evidence that a mapping landed, and the image column as supplied cannot bind anything until its shape is corrected.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholder inventory has been confirmed by inspection rather than by response text.

trajectory.action: Merge the twelve records one per page with the finished villa photographs bound per row, render at real print resolution through the render step, and read each rendered page at trim against its data row.
trajectory.judgement: The merge step ignores resolution on its own, multi record raster output cannot be trusted to come back in row order, and a page that renders is not the same as a page that carries its whole record.
trajectory.produces: One press document of twelve cards plus per record proofs, each read at trim against its row.

trajectory.action: Author the presentation as multiple roots at one canvas size and the booking pages and social set as roots at their own sizes, with every photograph inlined as image data, the welcome cutouts placed on the what is included panel on the Linen ground, the recovered cove mark placed as inline vector inside an explicitly sized wrapper anchored top left, the amenity lists and the rate ladder as real tables, type set over photography wherever the prestige look calls for it, and family and weight declared on every text element, then upload the files and hold the returned URLs.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents or the inline mark off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how much air the band buys and how a rate ladder stays discreet while a travel agency still sells from it.
trajectory.produces: Export ready HTML carrying the presentation, the booking pages and the social set, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve each document's rendition and look at its first canvas, and parse the returned per canvas markup for every canvas after the first.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition preview only ever shows the first artboard, so a six root presentation can be looked at exactly once and read no other way.
trajectory.produces: Native editable documents, an inspected first canvas each, and a per canvas markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Write the collection basis and the handover note: the photographic target and how it was reached per frame, the type system by role, what the card template actually contained, the data reconciliation, the cove mark recovery and its safe minimum reproduction height, the welcome cutout route per frame, and what to do when rates change.
trajectory.judgement: The note is the thing that survives the next rate change, so it has to be specific enough that the manager edits rather than re commissions.
trajectory.produces: The written collection basis and handover note.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the cut edge survives where a pale object meets the warm stone it is sitting on. The welcome things are shot on a villa's limestone, and on some frames the rose, the clear glass shoulder or the pale crust sit at almost the value of the stone. The knockout reports success, the returned cutout is complete and clean at thumbnail scale, and the bite only exists along the short stretch where the pale object and the stone share luminance. Which frames it happens to is a property of each frame's own light and the object's own colour, not of the object, and there is no confidence figure and no edge report anywhere in the response.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering does not dodge it, because the edge quality is a fact about this frame meeting this tool and exists only after the call has run and the result is looked at on the ground it will sit on, the Linen brand ground, not on white. Nothing states it: the brief says only that the welcome things were shot on the kitchen stone. And it is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different chain for the affected frames, a material named selection of the limestone, inverted and filled to the brand ground.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re plan the knockout route per frame, re derive the affected cutouts through the selection and fill chain, and re inspect every cutout against the Linen brand ground rather than against white.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A what is included panel and a season social set in which the welcome objects have a chewed edge along the glass or the crust on the frames nobody looked at closely, on a collection whose whole pitch is that nothing is a little bit wrong.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered cove mark is still the mark at the height it actually reproduces. The trace comes back looking correct: the headland and the cove and the roofline are there, the counters are open, and at full scan scale on a white page it is a faithful recovery. The foil printer stamps it across the corner of the card at roughly a thumbnail, and the glass etcher puts it on Maison Aubine's door at hand small, and at those heights the hairline tapers fill in and the cove mouth and the window openings close into solid blobs. The tracer takes no options at all, so nothing about the trace call can be tuned; the only evidence is placing the artwork at its real reproduction size on its real ground and looking.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the answer depends on the trace, the reproduction height and the ground colour being present together, and the first two are produced by the agent while the third is a property of the card stock and the glass. Nothing states it: the brief asks for a proper file the vendors can use and says the mark has to still look drawn by hand. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different raster preparation feeding the same tracer, a differently worded ink level selection, a fill and flatten plate instead of a binary mask, or a bounds crop that changes what the tracer sees, since the tracer itself has no lever.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re prepare the raster on a different route, re trace, re inject the viewBox and strip the opaque ground path again, then re place the result at reproduction height on the card stock and on the glass colour and re judge, and state a safe minimum height in the handover once one is actually known.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The founders' mark foil stamped on the card and etched on the door glass as a row of solid blobs, on the one mark the collection has and on pieces a guest paying 4,200 a night holds and walks through.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the licensed frame belongs to this collection. The search returns only a small CDN thumbnail, so the frame's true white balance, its own baked contrast, how its horizon sits and how its water reads all exist only after the licence is taken and the full resolution file is pulled down. Even then the question is not whether the frame is good, it is whether it sits with these three specific villas at their finished target, which cannot be answered until the two are finally adjacent on the opening root. Every step up to that point returns success: the search succeeded, the licence succeeded, the download succeeded, and the thumbnail looked right.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering does not avoid it, because the only order that would is licensing several candidates and comparing them at full resolution, which spends licences on a guess. Nothing states it: the brief never mentions a bought frame at all, it simply asks for a collection presentation, and the do not want list is the client's art direction rather than a warning about stock. And the response is not a re run, it is a decision between grading the licensed frame to the collection target, taking a second licence on a different candidate, and restructuring the opening root around a villa frame instead, each of which changes what the presentation opens on and therefore what the social end card carries.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re grade or re license, and if neither brings the frame inside the collection, re plan the opening root and the social end card around villa photography and re cut those crops.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A presentation whose first screen is visibly a bought photograph next to three carefully finished houses, shown to a travel agency by a collection whose whole pitch is consistency.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether every season note actually fits. The card's note frame is fixed at whatever size the printer set it, and a merged record longer than that does not spill, does not reflow and does not warn: it simply stops rendering at the frame edge, so the page comes back successfully with a sentence cut mid word at trim. Which record does it is a property of one villa's shoulder season note being two lines longer than the others, which is not visible from the data file's shape and cannot be predicted from the frame bounds without knowing what the printer's original specimen was.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the truncation happens at render and render is downstream of everything; and doing it right first time would require knowing the frame's capacity in set text, which no response reports and which the bounds alone do not give. Nothing states it: the client says only that the season note goes on the card. And it is not a propagation re run, because the response is a genuine choice, either changing the mapping so the note occupies a frame that can hold it, or editing the copy back to the frame with the manager's agreement, or re cutting the card's photograph panel to buy the note more room, and each choice changes a different deliverable.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re read every rendered page at trim rather than at thumbnail scale, decide the fix per the choice above, re prepare or re map, re merge the affected records, and re render and re read them.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Twelve cards printed and placed in the villas with one villa's shoulder season note ending mid sentence, on the one piece of collateral a guest paying 4,200 a night picks up and reads at arm's length.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the thing the prestige look is built on. The band's whole grammar is full bleed architecture with quiet type sitting over it, which is only legible if something softens the photograph under the words, and there are several plausible ways to author that: a semi opaque solid panel, a gradient with transparent stops, a blended overlay, a filtered backdrop. The importer keeps some of those and silently discards others, returns success either way, and says nothing about which. Whether what survives still holds the type against these specific photographs' brightness is visible only after the export, and the document's own rendition returns the first canvas only, so every villa root after the first can be read no other way than through the returned markup.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and import is the last step; and doing it right first time presumes knowing which construction survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. Nothing states it: the brief asks for a presentation and the acceptance line about legibility over photography is the client's own standard, not a warning. And it is not a propagation re run, because the response is to produce a different upstream asset or a different construction, for instance carrying the softening in the raster itself so it is part of the photograph, and then re composing the canvas around whichever it is.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re author the affected roots around a construction the importer keeps, or re derive the underlying frames so the softening lives in the raster, re upload, re run the readiness check, re export, and audit every canvas from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A presentation delivered as an editable document in which pale type sits unreadable over bright sky on the villa roots nobody could preview, with every export having reported success.

deliverables.name: Verranza collection photography
deliverables.spec: The full three villa set brought to one collection target: one white point, one black point, one treatment of stone and shadow, one relationship between interior and exterior brightness, with water that could exist at that hour and no fake high dynamic range look anywhere. The pre finished batch walked back rather than pushed further. Delivered with a per frame parameter log, the duplicate and shortfall reconciliation, and a named list of any frame that could not be brought to the collection, plus any licensed frame graded into the same world or explicitly excluded.

deliverables.name: In villa season card run, twelve records
deliverables.spec: Twelve cards, one villa and season per page, at the card's true trim, built from the printer's own artwork rather than a redrawn approximation: each carrying its own villa's finished photograph bound per record, its own rate, its own minimum stay written one consistent way, and its season note legible in full rather than stopped at a frame edge. Delivered as one press document plus per record proofs at real print resolution, with every field confirmed present by reading the rendered pages at trim.

deliverables.name: Portfolio presentation, booking pages and season social set
deliverables.spec: Native editable documents carrying the collection presentation across its roots, the three villa booking pages with the amenity list as a real table, and the season social canvases, each root keeping its own canvas size, with live retypeable text in one licensed type system, the rate ladder as a real table, type legible over photography on every canvas rather than only on the previewable one, and every photograph carried as embedded image data rather than a reference. The recovered cove mark is carried as real inline vector so it stays editable, and the welcome cutouts sit on the what is included panel on the Linen ground. Delivered with the self contained source HTML, which is the durable half: rates change twice a year and the source is what lets the manager edit rather than re commission.

deliverables.name: Collection welcome detail cutout set
deliverables.spec: The contractual welcome provision isolated onto the flat Linen brand ground at the size the what is included panel and the season social set give it: each object optically centred with clear air at every edge and a cut edge that holds where the pale object meets the warm limestone under close inspection rather than at thumbnail scale, with the returned resize record captured for each and no object standing in for two. One set with one cut logic, graded into the same collection world as the villa photography, not one object at several sizes.

deliverables.name: Recovered Anse Verranza cove mark
deliverables.spec: The hand inked cove motif recovered as placeable scalable artwork the foil printer and the glass etcher can use: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, delivered as a single colour stamping and etching version and a colour accurate variant, holding its hairline strokes and its small counters, the cove mouth and the roofline's window openings, at the height it is foil stamped on the card corner and etched on the door glass and on those grounds rather than on white, with a stated safe minimum height. Recovered from the supplied scan rather than redrawn, so it is still the founders' mark.

deliverables.name: Collection basis, handover note and owners' selects board
deliverables.spec: A written basis and note recording the photographic target and how each frame was brought to it, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight, every resize any tool reported, what the card template actually contained versus what the printed face suggested, the cove mark recovery and its safe minimum reproduction height, the welcome cutout route per frame, the data reconciliation across the twelve rows, and exactly what to change when rates move. Paired with a persistent shareable selects board the three owners sign off from, with nothing silently dropped.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are raster work, which need authored fixed canvas documents, and which need a record per page run, given that only one surface here does each.
Which frames arrived already finished, and the fact that those need walking back rather than pushing further, which is the opposite move from the rest of the set.
Where restraint stops being restraint and becomes a flat picture, on a set whose client has an explicit written list of what not to do.
Selection prompt wording throughout: naming the terrace or the villa takes the place, naming the material's own colour, surface and form takes the material.
Knockout route per welcome still life, between the one call subject knockout and a material named selection of the warm limestone inverted and filled, where a pale object and pale stone share value.
Selection wording on the cove mark scan: naming the paper takes the substrate, naming the ink's own visual properties takes the mark.

Whether the single colour stamping version or the colour accurate variant is what the foil printer and the glass etcher actually need, judged at foil stamp height on the card and etch height on the door glass rather than at full scan scale.
Whether a licensed frame joins this collection at all, judged at full resolution beside the finished villas rather than at thumbnail scale.
Whether the printer's card converts to separated frames or one continuous flow, and therefore whether the mapping is per frame or offset based inside one story.
What counts as proof that a mapping landed and that a record fits, given that both the validator and the render report success on a card with a sentence cut off.
How to reconcile twelve rows against three photographs and three differently written minimum stay values without inventing data.
Which construction carries type over full bleed photography, judged by what survives the import rather than by what looks right in a browser.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a milestone booking family comparing the collection to hotels, plus the real numeric weight per family.
How discreet the rate ladder can be while a travel agency can still sell from it. At this band understatement is the design and a benefit led grid is a correct looking wrong answer.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of a beautiful villa. IDENTITY: these are three specific houses that guests will physically arrive at, and a regenerated pool, terrace or view is a misrepresentation the manager can be held to, which is precisely why the do not want list exists and why they have lost bookings before. SPEC: twelve cards at the printer's trim, one villa and season per page, each field present in full, plus crops at fixed destinations with nothing enlarged, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: rates change twice a year and the client explicitly cannot re commission, so a flat render is worth nothing to them. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: is this water believable, does this bought frame belong here, does this note fit the frame, did the type survive the import on the roots nobody can preview, did this cutout bite the pale glass against the stone, does this trace still read as the founders' mark at foil stamp height. And the cove mark is a specific hand inked drawing that has to be RECOVERED rather than reinvented, because a regenerated mark is a different drawing in a different hand that the foil printer and the glass etcher cannot cut from a picture, while the welcome objects are the villa's own things isolated onto the collection's own ground, not stock still lifes.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_auto_tone, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, select_subject, invert_selection, remove_background in both the transparent and backgroundColor forms, fill_area, crop_to_bounds and crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection_confidence, and image_vectorize are all verified headless across 27 live calls, texture and material field selection is verified (a 672,398 pixel mask of a painted wood surface), and the documented HSL range holding only at moderate is exactly why a pre pushed frame has to be walked back rather than swung. The welcome cutout checkpoint rests on documented findings: remove_background needs one coherent blob, its edge behaviour is a property of the frame and the family reports no edge quality figure of any kind, and a material named selection of the surface inverted and filled is the verified alternative route. The cove mark checkpoint rests on the verified facts that image_vectorize takes NO options at all so all tuning is in the raster preparation, that naming the substrate returns the substrate, that background removal is the wrong instrument on inked strokes with counters, that the trace emits no viewBox, and that path index zero is always an opaque full canvas rectangle. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt as generator and validator, prepare_indd_merge_template with params.mappingJson as a JSON string, document_merge_data_layout with recordRange and additionalImageFiles, and document_render_layout at resolution 300 are verified headless and synchronous end to end, including a real per row image bind through an at prefixed CSV column and a verified one record per page PDF whose page count equals row count. The checkpoints rest on documented findings: Stock renditionURL is verified to be a 240px CDN thumbnail with true resolution only reachable through asset_license_and_download_stock (a real 7360x4912 JPEG was licensed and pulled); frame granularity from a PDF is verified as not under the author's control; and the importer is verified to DROP filter blur, backdrop-filter and mix-blend-mode entirely and to TRUNCATE multi layer box-shadow to layer one, all at HTTP success with no warning, while the rendition preview is documented as PAGE 1 ONLY, which is why verification is split between the rendition and the returned markup. EXPRESS: multiple roots in one export and mixed canvas sizes are verified, tables import as real tables with per cell strokes and text, gradients and single shadows survive, and transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined architectural photography passes the 70 KB threshold immediately. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end. BOARDS: persistence verified with a hard cap of 12 placements per call and 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no bleed claim on a PDF derived template, no pdfPreset, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text to image, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no fill_text, no animate_design, no batch above 20.
